# parity-fuzz --mode mathfunc baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode mathfunc --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (two seeds).
#
# Covers the user-defined math-function mechanism (c:Src/builtin.c bin_functions,
# c:Src/math.c callmathfunc) — extending the arithmetic evaluator's namespace at
# runtime, a path no arith-mode case reaches (arith only exercises operators).
#
# Float results print through the shell's own float formatter, which IS the
# parity question here, so they are deliberately not rounded away.
#
# The mode already existed and ran clean, but was NOT gated in CI, so nothing
# stopped a regression in it. Gating is what makes that clean run mean
# something. `trap` and `redir` sat in exactly this state and each turned out
# to be hiding real bugs once their vocabulary was widened — a clean ungated
# mode is an untested mode, not a correct one.
#
# The divergence this mode found was a real port bug and is FIXED:
#
#   `jn` and `yn` — the order-taking Bessel functions (c:144/168) — were
#   UNIMPLEMENTED on the live path:
#
#       $(( jn(1,0) ))   zsh 0.                zshrs unknown function: jn
#       $(( yn(1,1) ))   zsh -0.78121282...    zshrs unknown function: yn
#
#   c:Src/Modules/mathfunc.c:
#       NUMMATHFUNC("jn", math_func, 2, 2, MF_JN | TFLAG(TF_INT1)),
#       case MF_JN: retd = jn(argi, argd2); break;   /* c:333-335 */
#       NUMMATHFUNC("yn", math_func, 2, 2, MF_YN | TFLAG(TF_INT1))
#       case MF_YN: retd = yn(argi, argd2); break;   /* c:420-422 */
#   TF_INT1 (c:106) = the FIRST argument is the integer one — the mirror of
#   ldexp/scalb's TF_INT2, which the port already had.
#
#   TWO math-function tables exist. The faithful module port
#   (modules/mathfunc.rs) HAS jn/yn, with the right arity and TF_INT1 flags and
#   c: refs — and it is SHADOWED: the live evaluator is a second, inline table
#   in math.rs that carried j0/j1/y0/y1 but stopped short of the order-taking
#   forms. Same faithful-port-shadowed-by-a-reimplementation shape as
#   substnamedir / typeset_single / parse_string / dotrapargs / the four
#   subscript searches. The fix went into the live table.
#
#   The vocabulary is why it survived: C's module registers 49 functions and
#   this generator emitted 20. Of the 26 never generated, the two that were
#   broken were the only two taking an integer order. j0/j1/y0/y1 all worked,
#   so the family looked covered.
#
# Excluded deliberately:
#   rand48       nondeterministic by design (c:154)
#   signgam      a global set as a side effect of lgamma, not a pure function
#   isinf/isnan  the fork's table has them (c:140-141) but the 5.9.2 oracle
#                does not expose them — BOTH shells answer `unknown function`,
#                so they gate nothing. Same fork-ahead-of-oracle split as
#                `zstyle -q` / `zparseopts -G` / the `:S` modifier.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
